course_title: Spec. Topics in German Studies: Methods for Literary Research
subject: GER
course_description: Taught in English. An interdisciplinary course intended to provide in-depth study of formative elements, influences, and movements in German-speaking culture(s). May be repeated for credit when topic varies.
course_notes: (Same as CPLT 301 1) An introduction to the so-called "masters of the hermeneutics of suspicion," this course will provide a survey of the contributions of Freud, Marx, and Nietzsche to literary interpretation. Each of these thinkers are credited with producing new ways of reading, but what does it mean to describe an interpretation as "Marxist," "Nietzschean" or "Freudian"? By the end of this course students should be able to identify the key features of these styles of interpretation and be able to apply these ways of reading to works of literature and other media. This course will also provide context for the significance of all three thinkers for 20th and 21st century developments in psychoanalytic theory, historical materialism, modernist and post-modernist literary theory, aesthetics, and cultural studies.
